Estudiamos cómo la inferencia local en dispositivos móviles puede reducir la dependencia de la nube sin comprometer los resultados, e identificamos retos como la evaluación realista, la integración en el flujo de trabajo y las restricciones de cómputo, memoria y energía.

title: Design and Development of an AI-Powered Intelligent Chatbot for Student Information Services in Higher Educational Institutions Using Large Language Models
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science and Technology
authors: OHIA Paul Ndudiri; Joseph Bamikole Olojido
keywords: chatbots; student information services; retrieval-augmented generation; large language models; higher education institutions; polytechnics; university administration; user satisfaction
topics: AI in Service Interactions; Artificial Intelligence in Education; Speech and dialogue systems
abstract: Higher educational institutions increasingly face pressure to respond quickly and consistently to routine student enquiries on admissions, registration, examinations, course requirements, and institutional policies. This study designed, developed, and evaluated an AI-powered chatbot for student information services using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. Institutional documents, including the student handbook, admission guidelines, frequently asked questions, and course catalogue, were pre-processed into retrievable knowledge chunks and connected to a Large Language Model through a Flask-based backend and browser-based chat interface. A formative pilot evaluation was conducted with 30 volunteer participants, comprising 24 undergraduate students and 6 administrative or academic-affairs staff. Across 120 test queries, 94 responses were rated fully correct, 19 partially correct, and 7 incorrect or irrelevant, giving a combined fully/substantially correct response rate of 94.2%. The chatbot returned responses in an average of 3.8 seconds under normal network conditions, while 82.0% of satisfaction ratings were 4 or 5 on a five-point Likert scale. Only 9 of the 120 queries, representing 7.5%, required fallback or escalation to human staff because they were ambiguous, sensitive, or outside the available knowledge base. The findings indicate that combining Large Language Models with RAG-grounded institutional content can improve the availability, responsiveness, and consistency of routine student information services in Nigerian polytechnic and university contexts, provided the knowledge base is regularly updated and human escalation remains available for complex cases.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation LLM Chatbot with Structured Database Access
authors: Juan Burbano Bonifaz; Pablo Landeta-López; Cathy Guevara‐Vega; Antonio Quiña‐Mera
keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; large language models; chatbots; grocery stores; inventory management; text-to-SQL; Mistral-7B-Instruct; small retailers; online grocery shopping
topics: AI in Service Interactions; Topic Modeling; Speech and dialogue systems
abstract: Context. The grocery sector is undergoing a massive shift in consumer behavior, with global chatbot usage projected to reach 8.4 billion units by 2024—surpassing the total human population—and online grocery revenue per shopper expected to hit USD 449.00 by 2023. In this competitive landscape, small grocery stores must adopt AI-driven tools to modernize their operations. However, these businesses often face significant inefficiencies in manual inventory management, resulting in errors and reduced competitiveness. Objective. This research aims to develop and validate a chatbot application using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for operational management of grocery stores. Method. The method employed a quantitative experimental approach with a five-component system architecture: a web interface, a FastAPI API, a Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 model, a dynamic SQL generator, and a custom RAG application with an FAISS vector database, all integrated through SQLAlchemy 2.0.40. Results. The results demonstrate that a chatbot achieves an average response time of 0.08 s with 80% overall accuracy, showing a 96.2% improvement in information query time and a 92.9% reduction in operational errors. Conclusions. Major conclusions suggest that the chatbot system is effective for retail environments and has the potential to enhance the operational efficiency of grocery stores, serving as a foundation for future research in applied conversational assistance.

title: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Agent Architectures for Stock Price Prediction: A Vietnam Case Study
authors: Duong Nguyen Minh; Dat Nguyen Huu
keywords: stock price prediction; multi-agent systems; ensemble voting; hierarchical coordination; retail investors; investor sentiment; emerging stock markets; Vietnamese stock market; forecast horizon; Diebold-Mariano test
topics: Stock Market Forecasting Methods; Financial Markets and Investment Strategies; Forecasting Techniques and Applications
abstract: Stock price prediction in emerging markets is complicated by retail investor dominance, sentiment-driven volatility, and settlement constraints. We evaluate a multi-agent forecasting framework tailored to Vietnam’s market, where retail investors account for approximately 85–90% of total trading volume. The system deploys six specialised agents covering technical, fundamental, risk, sentiment, macroeconomic, and microstructure signals, coordinated through three mechanisms—Hierarchical, Round Robin, and Ensemble Voting—and evaluated across three LLM backbones (Gemini 2.0 Flash, GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-8B) on twelve stocks across six sectors. Ensemble Voting achieves the lowest aggregate MAPE at all three horizons (3.34%, 4.97%, 8.06%), with statistically significant advantages over Hierarchical at medium- and long-term horizons and a marginal advantage at the short-term horizon ( $p = 0.052$ ), and over Round Robin at medium- and long-term horizons (Diebold–Mariano $p \leq 0.098$ and $p \leq 0.083$ respectively). LLM selection is horizon-dependent: Llama-3.1-8B performs best at short horizons, Gemini 2.0 Flash at long horizons ( $p = 0.027$ vs. Llama), and GPT-4o and Gemini perform comparably at medium-term horizons ( $p = 0.838$ ). The multi-agent framework reduces MAPE by 75.4%, 63.3%, and 42.3% over single-agent LLMs at 3-day, 14-day, and 60-day horizons respectively (DM $p \lt 0.001$ at short- and medium-term; $p \leq 0.015$ at long-term). This advantage is conditional on information-regime complexity and narrows in stable, policy-anchored regimes, providing a statistically grounded basis for horizon-adaptive architecture and LLM selection in emerging market forecasting.

title: Design and implementation of a local LLM-driven decision support system for AI-enhanced supply chain management
authors: Kelvin K. L. Wong; Liurui Deng; Yingge Liu; Yingge Liu; Jie Tu
keywords: large language models; decision support system; supply chain management; Ollama; supplier evaluation; inventory planning; distribution requirements planning; production logistics; natural language interaction; query routing; privacy-preserving AI; forecasting models
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society; Supply Chain and Inventory Management; Decision Support System Applications
abstract: This paper presents a large language model (LLM) decision support system for supply chain management (SCM). Building on a multi-layer architecture originally developed for intelligent manufacturing planning, the proposed artificial intelligence (Al) system is re-engineered to address end-to-end SCM tasks including supplier evaluation, inventory planning, production logistics, and distribution planning. A 14-billion-parameter LLM is deployed on-premise via the Ollama framework, allowing natural-language interaction while ensuring that sensitive SCM data remain within the local computing environment. The system integrates multiple knowledge sources – formal SCM theory, standardised process maps, structured supplier and inventory databases, and empirically calibrated forecasting models – into a single, query-driven decision pipeline. A classification module distinguishes theoretical, analytical, and procedural queries and routes them to appropriate deterministic models and knowledge bases before the LLM generates explanations. Through automated context construction and domain-restricted prompting, the AI agent produces technically validated, context-aware responses suitable for interactive planning. Experimental deployments on realistic SCM scenarios indicate that the system can provide rapid supplier scoring, inventory parameter tuning, DRP-based distribution planning, and policy comparisons with transparent, database-grounded justifications. The results demonstrate that combining local LLMs with classical decision models offers a practical path toward trustworthy, privacy-preserving AI decision support for both industrial SCM environments.

title: Cyber-Physical Internet-Enabled Spatial-Temporal Traceability for Production Logistics Synchronization: An Agentic Reasoning Approach
authors: Jinpeng Li; Zhiheng Zhao; George Q. Huang
keywords: discrete manufacturing; agentic reasoning; multi-agent systems; large language models; hallucination mitigation; data fusion; information retrieval; personalized production; zero inventory
topics: Digital Transformation in Industry; Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society; Applied Advanced Technologies
abstract: In discrete manufacturing, the growing demand for personalized production has significantly increased process complexity and placed higher requirements on production logistics (PL). To achieve zero inventory and even zero warehousing, PL synchronization has become increasingly important, since it ensures that operators, tools, and materials are available at the required location within a specified time window, thereby enabling production, assembly, and transportation activities to start and finish as planned. In this context, spatial-temporal traceability is essential for tracking PL resources and determining their availability in time and space. Recently, the Cyber-Physical Internet (CPI) has provided a promising foundation for connecting physical and digital entities and supporting real-time information sharing. However, relevant traceability information is often fragmented and stored across various CPI routers, which makes its collection, integration, and analysis highly challenging. Meanwhile, although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in information understanding and reasoning, they remain prone to hallucinations and may lack reliability in complex industrial decision-making scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an agentic reasoning approach for spatial-temporal traceability. The approach introduces multiple function-specific agents to handle tasks such as information retrieval, data fusion, and stakeholder-oriented query support. Through collaboration among these agents, it improves the accuracy, coherence, and interpretability of traceability reasoning over fragmented data, thereby enabling different stakeholders to obtain the spatial-temporal information they need through CPI more effectively.

title: CuraVox: An AI-Powered Mobile Medical Assistant for Visually Impaired Users Using a Hybrid LLM and OCR Pipeline
source: Journal of Computer Based Parallel Programming
authors: G. Kruthika; K. Kavya; K. Swathi; Kayam Sai Krishna; S. K Hiremath; B. K Deshpande
keywords: visually impaired users; medication management; tablet identification; optical character recognition; large language models; vision-language models; mobile accessibility; text-to-speech; speech-to-text; medication reminders; on-device inference; Ollama; Google Gemini; haptic feedback; voice assistants
topics: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility; Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education; Mobile Health and mHealth Applications
abstract: CuraVox is a fully implemented AI-powered mobile pharmaceutical assistant designed for visually impaired users. In order to minimize confusion, the assistant uses VLM and LLM to identify tablets by examining their form, color, and imprints. Barcodes, safety information, and expiration dates are instantly identified via barcodes, QR scanning, and certain systems. Customizable warnings for taking medication on time are part of integrated systems. The technologies to be used include Flutter and React Native for front-end (mobile), TalkBack and VoiceOver for accessibility, and FastAPI and Flask Cloud APIs for back-end Python. Tesseract and Google ML Kit are the AI Stack OCRs. The GPT/LLaMA and speech via text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT) are the LLMs. The application integrates a camera-based optical character recognition (OCR) pipeline, a hybrid large language model (LLM) reasoning layer using Google Gemini 2.0 Flash, and a local Ollama fallback, proactive text-to-speech (TTS) narration via expo-speech, haptic confirmation via expo-haptics; and a drug interaction checker supporting up to five concurrent medications. A prescription image vault, and medication reminders, all within a single React Native / Expo mobile application backed by a Python FastAPI asynchronous REST API. The system auto-scans medicine labels every four seconds, identifies medicine name, dosage, manufacturer, expiry date, clinical insight, safety flags, indications, and side effects, and narrates the complete result aloud without any user interaction. In cloud mode, response latency averages 1.2 seconds with approximately 97% medicine identification accuracy. In offline mode, the system operates with 100% data privacy using on-device Ollama inference. A voice agent module powered by @react-native-voice and a backend Gemini NLU layer enables completely hands-free navigation across all application features. This paper presents the complete system design, architecture, implementation details, API specification, and evaluation results.

title: Από τις φόρμες CRUD στον διάλογο : αντικαθιστώντας τις παραδοσιακές εφαρμογές forms-over-data με conversational agents καθοδηγούμενους από LLM
authors: Νικόλαος Κωστόπουλος
keywords: chatbots; large language models; natural language interfaces; intent classification; structured output; error recovery; cross-model evaluation; TypeScript library; prompt caching; business applications; obfuscation
topics: Speech and dialogue systems; Web Applications and Data Management; AI in Service Interactions
abstract: A surprising fraction of every business application running on the modern web is,-in essence, a form: a sequence of validated, conditionally-routed, externally-bound-fields that the user fills out and the system stores as a record. Such forms-overdata-applications combine deterministic state, navigation, and actions with a user-experience well known to suffer --- abandonment rates near seventy percent in-published checkout studies --- and a developer experience dominated by configuration-sprawl, validation duplication, and per-page state management. This thesis examines whether Large Language Models can replace the form's user-interface without sacrificing the determinism that makes a form a useful component-of a business system. The argument defended is a hybrid one: keep the deterministic-machinery of state, navigation, and action in classical software, where it has-always belonged; delegate only the natural-language understanding step --- intent-classification, field extraction, response generation --- to an LLM, but constrain it-through structured output, a closed action taxonomy, and a configuration-driven-schema generated at request time. The thesis presents the Agent Engine, a configuration-driven, framework-agnostic-engine that realises this architecture as a four-phase iterative validation loop-with two-tier validation, two-tier error recovery, and a uniform tool protocol. The-engine is implemented as a single-file TypeScript library (@nkostop/agentengine),-exercised by a declarative JSON scenario corpus, and shipped through an-encrypt-and-obfuscate build pipeline. A bilingual (Greek and English) bank-branch-appointment-booking case study is exhibited as a complete configuration (32 kB, 598-lines), a set of TypeScript handlers (535 filtered lines of code), and a corpus of mock-scenarios (twenty scenarios, sixty turns). The evaluation reports four kinds of result. A real cross-model evaluation suite over-nineteen Large Language Models with two rounds of agent-configuration optimisation-shows three frontier models reaching one-hundred-percent suite pass rate and six-more reaching ninety-five to ninety-eight percent. The case-study deliverable lands-at approximately half to a third of the size of the estimated React-stack baseline. Per-booking cost projections place the case study under five US cents per booking-on prompt-cached small-model deployments, with annual operating cost of roughly-nine thousand US dollars at the documented case-study volume of ten thousand-bookings per week. A controlled user study with real participants is identified as the-next empirical round. Throughout, every metric is tagged as a measurement or a-projection, and the boundary between the two is named explicitly. The thesis closes by acknowledging the conditions under which forms remain the right-answer (high-frequency power users, latency-critical contexts, regulatory transcripts,-accessibility- sensitive deployments, among others), the LLM-tier failure modes the-engine mitigates only partially, the security and privacy considerations regulated-deployments must address, and the broader ethical concerns --- bias in extraction,-displacement of human service agents, the false-friend user experience, dark-pattern-risk --- that no technical choice eliminates. Five directions for future work are-sketched: multi-modal input, adaptive prompt optimisation, agent composition,-on-device deployment, and automated continuous evaluation.

title: Cross-Domain Explainable AI for Customer Recommendations, Fraud Detection, and Network Intelligence
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Nivedan Suresh Abhignan Srivatsava Sribhashyam; Supraja Ayyamgari
keywords: explainable AI; decision support system; multi-agent systems; retrieval-augmented generation; customer recommendation; inventory optimization; fraud detection; financial risk assessment; network anomaly detection; intelligent traffic management; SHAP; lime; causal inference; responsible AI
topics: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI); Artificial Intelligence Applications; Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled Decision Support Systems (DSS) have become fundamental components of modern enterprise ecosystems, facilitating intelligent automation across customer engagement, financial risk management, and network operations. Despite remarkable advances in deep learning and Large Language Models (LLMs), the opaque nature of these models presents significant challenges in terms of explainability, trustworthiness, accountability, and regulatory compliance, limiting their adoption in mission-critical decision-making environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an Explainable Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence Framework for Decision Intelligence (XMAI-DI), a unified cross-domain architecture that integrates collaborative intelligent agents, retrieval-augmented enterprise knowledge, and explainable AI techniques to generate transparent, reliable, and auditable decision outcomes. The proposed framework employs specialized autonomous agents dedicated to customer recommendation and inventory optimization, fraud detection and financial risk assessment, and network anomaly detection and intelligent traffic management. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) module enriches agent reasoning by dynamically incorporating enterprise knowledge repositories, while an Explainability Orchestration Layer combines SHAP-based global feature attribution, LIME-based local explanations, causal inference, and governance-aware auditing to provide comprehensive and human-interpretable decision justifications. Furthermore, an adaptive orchestration mechanism coordinates inter-agent communication, confidence estimation, and knowledge refinement to improve decision consistency and operational scalability across heterogeneous enterprise environments. Experimental evaluation across representative retail, financial, and networking scenarios demonstrates that the proposed framework significantly improves decision transparency, interpretability, operational efficiency, and governance compliance while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The integration of explainable reasoning, collaborative multi-agent intelligence, and enterprise knowledge retrieval establishes a scalable foundation for trustworthy next-generation Decision Support Systems capable of supporting responsible AI deployment in complex cross-domain enterprise applications.

title: CodeBuddy: A Browser-Based Platform for Learning Data Structures and Algorithms Using AI-Driven Feedback
source: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
authors: N. Ramanaiah; K. Satya Krishna Chowdary; P. Sowjanya; M. Anish Kumar
keywords: data structures and algorithms education; AI-driven feedback; large language models; DeepSeek-Coder; productive failure; code validation
topics: Teaching and Learning Programming; Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning; Artificial Intelligence in Education
abstract: Abstract—Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) remains one of the most challenging subjects in undergraduate computer science education. Students frequently struggle not because the concepts are inherently impossible, but because the feedback available to them is either absent or counterproductive. Most online platforms report only whether code passed or failed without explaining why, while unrestricted AI tools tend to hand over complete answers before students have had a genuine opportunity to think. This paper presents CodeBuddy, a lightweight, browser-based DSA practice environment that uses the DeepSeek-Coder large language model to provide intelligent, structured assistance to learners as they work through problems. The platform hosts 70 carefully designed problems spanning 7 core topics, with support for Python, JavaScript, Java, C, and C++. Its central feature is an attempt-gating mechanism: students must submit at least two attempts before hints become available, and at least four before a full solution is accessible. This design draws on established learning science research and is intended to encourage genuine engagement with each problem rather than reaching for help at the first sign of difficulty. The system additionally provides real-time error analysis, time and space complexity feedback, and a six-tier progressive hint system that guides thinking without replacing it. Early observations indicate that the graduated approach nudges students toward deeper reasoning before assistance is sought. Keywords—Data Structures and Algorithms, AI-Powered Education, Large Language Models, Progressive Hints, Code Validation, DSA Practice Platform, Productive Failure, DeepSeek-Coder

title: “Cognitive Sandwich” architecture for LLM agents in logistics
source: Digitalen Hochschulbibliothek Sachsen-Anhalt (Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek Sachsen-Anhalt)
authors: Maksim Ilin; Dmitry Pavlyuk
keywords: LLM agents; LLM hallucination; supply chain management; digital twin; decision support system; multi-agent systems; supply chain disruption; logistics
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society; Multi-Agent Systems and Negotiation; Supply Chain Resilience and Risk Management
abstract: Traditional decision support systems in supply chain management often lack the flexibility to handle unpredictable disruptions, while emerging autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) struggle with hallucination risks and a lack of mathematically guaranteed plans. To address this challenge, this paper proposes the "Cognitive Sandwich" architecture, a hybrid method that surrounds the LLM's semantic reasoning with strict, deterministic constraints. By utilizing the Model Context Protocol, this approach grounds the agent's decision-making in real-world data from a digital twin and validates it through a mathematical solver. Our experimental results, based on testing across 78 port infrastructure degradation scenarios, confirm the architecture's effectiveness. During these tests, we also identified and classified specific behavioral errors in LLM agents, such as "cognitive escape" (attempting to invent unauthorized network routes) and "Stubborn Agent Syndrome" (falling into infinite loops when attempting to iteratively resolve strict mathematical constraints). From a practical perspective, this verified architecture establishes a strong foundation for building reliable and auditable multi-agent systems in logistics, representing a crucial step toward intelligent, adaptable supply chain orchestration under high uncertainty.

title: COLLAB-LLM: A Communication-Centric Role-Based Framework for Scalable Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
source: Asian Journal of Research in Computer Science
authors: Elham Albaroudi; Mohammad Hatamleh; Sirin Mohammed Hejazi; Ahmad Yasser Alshalabi; Taha Mansouri; Ali Alameer
keywords: agent coordination; negotiation; scalability; software engineering tasks; business process automation
topics: Multi-Agent Systems and Negotiation; Natural Language Processing Techniques; AI-based Problem Solving and Planning
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems; however, existing frameworks continue to suffer from communication ambiguity, coordination failures, and poor scalability as task complexity increases. This paper introduces COLLAB-LLM, a communication-centric, role-based framework designed to enable reliable and scalable collaboration among LLM agents. The framework combines a structured communication protocol, a hierarchical role architecture, and a dynamic distributed task-graph engine to support coordinated planning, efficient negotiation, and adaptive task execution. COLLAB-LLM is evaluated on over 120 complex, multi-step tasks spanning software engineering, business process automation, and scientific research synthesis. Task success is defined using task-specific completion criteria, with a task considered successful when the aggregate completion score exceeds 0.8. Under identical underlying LLM configurations, COLLAB-LLM achieves an 89% overall success rate, representing a 13–19% improvement over strong single-agent and multi-agent state-of-the-art baselines, with statistically significant gains in performance, communication efficiency, and robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that structured communication and role specialization substantially reduce ambiguity, improve collaboration quality, and enable scalable coordination for teams of up to eight agents. This work establishes foundational design principles for high-performing collaborative AI systems and provides a practical, reproducible pathway toward scalable, human-aligned multi-agent LLM architectures. All experimental artifacts, task definitions, prompts, and evaluation scripts will be released to support reproducibility.

title: Collaborative Inference and Learning between Edge SLMs and Cloud LLMs: A Survey of Algorithms, Execution, and Open Challenges
authors: Senyang Li; Haozhao Wang; Wenchao Xu; Rui Zhang; Song Guo; Jingling Yuan; Xian Zhong; Tianwei Zhang; Ruixuan Li
keywords: cloud-edge collaboration; small language models; large language models; collaborative inference; collaborative training; task offloading; speculative decoding; pruning; distributed adaptation; privacy-preserving inference; edge computing; cloud computing
topics: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Topic Modeling; Advanced Neural Network Applications
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve, deploying them solely in the cloud or compressing them for edge devices is increasingly inadequate due to latency, privacy, cost, and personalization concerns. This survey examines a collaborative paradigm in which cloud-based LLMs and edge-deployed small language models (SLMs) cooperate for both inference and training. We propose a unified taxonomy of edge-cloud collaboration strategies. For inference, we categorize approaches into task assignment, task division, and mixture-based collaboration at both task- and token-levels, encompassing adaptive scheduling, resource-aware offloading, speculative decoding, and modular routing. For training, we review distributed adaptation techniques, including parameter alignment, pruning, bidirectional distillation, and small-model-guided optimization. We further summarize datasets, benchmarks, and deployment practices, and highlight privacy-preserving methods and vertical applications. This survey aims to establish a systematic foundation for LLM-SLM collaboration, bridging system-algorithm co-design toward efficient, scalable, and trustworthy edge-cloud intelligence.

title: Collaborative Knowledge Editing for Large Language Model Services in Edge-Cloud Computing
authors: Guozeng Xu; Xiuhua Li; Junhao Wen; Qiang He; Xiaofei Wang; Victor C. M. Leung
keywords: knowledge editing; large language models; edge servers; edge-cloud computing; knowledge forgetting; overfitting; federated fine-tuning
topics: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Topic Modeling; Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data
abstract: With the rapid deployment of large language model (LLM) technology across various fields, numerous LLMs have been deployed on edge servers (ESs) to provide low-latency generative services for edge devices. However, as factual knowledge evolves, the massive number of parameters in LLMs poses significant challenges for updating LLMs on ESs. Existing studies employ federated fine-tuning to update LLMs, but these unconstrained updating approaches can lead to overfitting and knowledge forgetting, while also resulting in substantial overhead. Knowledge editing (KE), as a promising technology, ensures the injection of new knowledge while preserving existing knowledge by editing specific parameters. In this paper, we propose multi-ES collaborative KE for the first time and design the CoKE and pCoKE frameworks in edge-cloud scenarios. These frameworks enhance editing efficiency by extracting identical expressions of the same knowledge across different LLM parameters for collaborative editing across multiple ESs. Additionally, we incorporate a personalized selection module in pCoKE to provide domain-specific generative services on ESs. To further reduce editing latency, we design a binary search-based resource allocation algorithm to balance editing latency across ESs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoKE and pCoKE reduce editing latency by 73% while maintaining high editing quality. Moreover, pCoKE achieves an approximately 6% improvement in editing quality.

title: COMFORT: A Continual Fine-Tuning Framework for Foundation Models Targeted at Consumer Healthcare
source: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
authors: Chia‐Hao Li; Niraj Jha
keywords: wearable medical sensors; disease detection; foundation models; continual fine-tuning; parameter-efficient fine-tuning; low-rank adaptation; transformer pre-training; physiological signals; edge devices; memory efficiency; multi-disease detection; early-stage disease detection
topics: Non-Invasive Vital Sign Monitoring; Machine Learning in Healthcare; Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning
abstract: Wearable medical sensors (WMSs) are revolutionizing smart healthcare by enabling continuous, real-time monitoring of user physiological signals, especially in the field of consumer healthcare. The integration of WMSs and modern machine learning enables unprecedented solutions to efficient early-stage disease detection. Despite the success of Transformers in various fields, their application to sensitive domains, such as smart healthcare, remains underexplored due to limited data accessibility and privacy concerns. A key challenge in disease detection using Transformers with WMS data is the difficulty of obtaining sufficient labeled training data from individuals suffering from a specific disease, as this requires labeling by experts and extensive time and effort devoted to data collection and data privacy regulation compliance. The phrase “foundation models” conjures up an image of a large language model trained on text corpora. However, foundation models need not be large, nor necessarily trained on text. In this work, we propose a foundation model trained on WMS data under a continual fine-tuning framework called COMFORT. COMFORT introduces a novel approach for pre-training a Transformer-based foundation model on a large dataset of physiological signals exclusively collected from healthy individuals with commercially available WMSs. We adopt a masked data modeling (MDM) objective to pre-train this health foundation model. MDM is inspired by the mask language modeling approach employed in self-supervised training of language models. Our WMS-based foundation model can then be rapidly adapted to multiple disease detection tasks through various parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, such as Low-Rank Adaptation and its variants. COMFORT continually stores the low-rank decomposition matrices and classifiers obtained using the PEFT algorithms to construct a library for multi-disease detection. This library enables scalable and memory-efficient disease detection on edge devices. Our experimental results demonstrate that COMFORT achieves highly competitive performance while reducing memory overhead by up to 52% relative to conventional methods. Thus, COMFORT paves the way for personalized and proactive solutions to efficient and effective early-stage disease detection.

title: Communication-Efficient Hybrid Language Model via Uncertainty-Aware Opportunistic and Compressed Transmission
authors: Sung-Nam Oh; Jinhyuk Kim; Jihong Park; Seung‐Woo Ko; Jinho D. Choi; Tony Q. S. Quek; Seong‐Lyun Kim
keywords: hybrid language models; communication efficiency; uncertainty threshold; token throughput; opportunistic transmission; heterogeneous distributed computing
topics: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Natural Language Processing Techniques; Topic Modeling
abstract: To support emerging language-based applications using dispersed and heterogeneous computing resources, the hybrid language model (HLM) offers a promising architecture, where an on-device small language model (SLM) generates draft tokens that are validated and corrected by a remote large language model (LLM). However, the original HLM suffers from substantial communication overhead, as the LLM requires the SLM to upload the full vocabulary distribution for each token. Moreover, both communication and computation resources are wasted when the LLM validates tokens that are highly likely to be accepted. To overcome these limitations, we proposecommunication-efficient and uncertainty-aware HLM (CU-HLM). In CU-HLM, the SLM transmits truncated vocabulary distributions only when its output uncertainty is high. We validate the feasibility of this opportunistic transmission by discovering a strong correlation between SLM’s uncertainty and LLM’s rejection probability. Furthermore, we theoretically derive optimal uncertainty thresholds and optimal vocabulary truncation strategies. Simulation results show that, compared to standard HLM, CU-HLM achieves up to 206× higher token throughput by skipping 74.8% transmissions with 97.4% vocabulary compression, while maintaining 97.4% accuracy.

title: Application of AI Agentic Workflow Algorithms in Contemporary Business Process Automation
source: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Technology Information (JAITI)
authors: Dita Novita Sari; Ricco Herdiyan Saputra
keywords: multi-agent reinforcement learning; business process automation; robotic process automation; fault tolerance; self-correction; enterprise resource planning; large language models
topics: Robotic Process Automation Applications; Business Process Modeling and Analysis; Artificial Intelligence Applications
abstract: Contemporary business process automation faces a critical anomaly: conventional Robotic Process Automation (RPA) frameworks often experience fatal runtime crashes when encountering minor structural variations in enterprise documents. This instability triggers severe operational bottlenecks and exponentially increases manual intervention costs. To resolve this fragility, this study proposes and evaluates a novel AI Agentic Workflow architecture based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning. The dynamic system orchestrates specialized sub-agents, specifically Planning, Tool-Execution, and Self-Reflection agents, to enable autonomous fault tolerance and contextual reasoning without relying on rigid scripts. Experimental testing was conducted across standard, structural drift, and ambiguous input scenarios using 5,000 synthetic and real-world supply chain documents. The empirical results demonstrate that the multi-agent architecture drastically outperforms legacy RPA and single-prompt Large Language Models, achieving a 98.9% Task Success Rate under severe structural drift. Furthermore, the system recorded a 99.2% Error Self-Correction Efficiency, successfully resolving runtime faults autonomously without human triage. Although the cognitive reasoning loops introduced an increased mean latency of 19.8 seconds, the computational trade-off is justified by the elimination of technical debt. Ultimately, this framework ensures highly adaptive enterprise resource planning ecosystems, safeguarding business continuity against unpredictable data fluctuations and volatile external integrations.

title: Comparing LLM Architectures in Street Fighter III
authors: Andrew Hinh; Hyemin Doo; Jack Wu
keywords: large language models; vision-language models
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Games; Artificial Intelligence Applications; Natural Language Processing Techniques
abstract: We built a browser-based Street Fighter III benchmark for comparing large language models (LLMs) and visionlanguage models (VLMs) under real-time constraints. The game runs through a Gymnasium-like control loop that exposes both frames and structured state while the agent emits button actions. We deploy the system on Modal and stream matches overWebRTC, which lets us compare ability, latency, and cost in one setting instead of spreading them across unrelated benchmarks. Because the benchmark is narrow, architectural tradeoffs that are easy to blur in offline evaluation show up quickly during live play.

title: Contextual Fusion Strategies for Multimodal GNN-Based Reasoning: Performance and Computational Trade-Offs
authors: Sanggeon Yun; Ryozo Masukawa; Raheeb Hassan; Minhyoung Na; Mohsen Imani
keywords: multimodal fusion; graph neural networks; knowledge graphs; video anomaly detection; feature-level fusion; decision fusion; energy efficiency; edge deployment; resource-constrained devices; mission-critical applications
topics: Anomaly Detection Techniques and Applications; Advanced Graph Neural Networks; Multimodal Machine Learning Applications
abstract: The integration of multimodal data is essential for mission-specific tasks requiring comprehensive reasoning across diverse information sources, especially in resource-constrained environments. MissionGNN, a hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework, has shown promise in deploying complex task models on edge devices by leveraging knowledge graphs (KGs). However, optimizing the fusion of different modalities remains a key challenge, as it significantly impacts the trade-off between computational efficiency and performance accuracy. In this paper, we propose three novel knowledge graph-centric fusion strategies for multimodal video anomaly detection within a hierarchical GNN-based reasoning framework—KG-based early fusion, late fusion,andreasoning fusion—along withmodality-aware knowledge graph generationto enhance modality-specific reasoning. Extensive experiments on the XD-Violence dataset evaluate their trade-offs across performance, computational cost, energy consumption, and LLM-basedKGgeneration cost. Early knowledge fusion offers a balanced solution, achieving significant accuracy improvements while reducing energy consumption by over 70% per frame. Late knowledge fusion, using half-sized modality-aware KGs, further improves accuracy with a modest increase in computational costs. Reasoning fusion achieves the highest accuracy of 72.93% mAP, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance, though it incurs higher resource usage. These results provide valuable insights for designing efficient multimodal GNN-based reasoning systems. By exploring these trade-offs, our work offers a framework to guide practitioners in selecting fusion strategies that balance energy efficiency and task-specific accuracy, tailored to mission-critical applications and varying resource constraints.

title: Conversational AI for inventory analytics: Leveraging large language models in supply chain management
authors: Oussama Zabraoui; Yahya Hmamou; Anas Chafi; Salaheddine Kammouri Alami
keywords: conversational AI; large language models; supply chain management; natural language querying; inventory forecasting; non-technical users; Llama 4; FastAPI backend; inventory tracking

title: Conversational Commerce and Inclusive Digital Retailing in Tier-2 and Tier-3 Cities: Redefining the Indian Rural-Urban Retail Interface
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH AND ANALYTICAL REVIEWS
authors: Dr. Dayanand Parappa Bellagi
keywords: conversational commerce; Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities; e-commerce adoption; digital inclusion; Indian retail sector
topics: Consumer Retail Behavior Studies; Digital Innovation in Industries; AI in Service Interactions
abstract: The rapid evolutionary trajectory of digital technologies has fundamentally restructured the retail landscape, particularly within emerging market economies where conversational commerce is shifting how enterprises engage with consumers.In India, Tier-2 and Tier-3 urban clusters have transformed into primary engines of digital economic growth.This transition is heavily driven by affordable smartphone access, low-cost mobile data infrastructure, robust digital payment networks, and targeted state-led financial inclusion programs.Conversational commerce-defined as the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Large Language Models (LLMs), automated chatbots, voice assistants, and messaging platforms-allows retailers to offer personalized product recommendations, real-time customer care, and integrated transactional flows.This paper examines the systemic role of conversational commerce in cultivating an inclusive digital retailing framework within Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.Using a conceptual research methodology built on recent academic literature, policy documentation, and industry insights up to 2026, this study examines the technological components, business opportunities, operational friction points, and policy implications of AI-driven retail networks.The paper argues that conversational commerce functions as an agent of digital democratization.It systematically reduces technological barriers and expands market access to empower micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), traditional Kirana counters, and women entrepreneurs.Despite persistent challenges involving digital literacy disparities, language variance, privacy vulnerabilities, and infrastructural inconsistencies, conversational commerce provides a scalable pathway toward an equitable and resilient retail landscape.The study concludes with actionable strategic recommendations for localized multilingual language modeling, user interface optimization, and public-private tech initiatives designed to accelerate inclusive digital transformation.

title: CPIAE: Arquitectura Python No Bloqueante Basada en Edge Computing para la Educación en Programación Asistida por IA con Retroalimentación Contextual
authors: Guillermo Sentoni
keywords: edge computing; Web Workers; Pyodide; WebAssembly; prompt engineering; context-aware feedback
topics: Teaching and Learning Programming; Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning; Mobile and Web Applications
abstract: This paper presents CPIAE, an edge-based architecture that delivers scientific Python environments as self-contained web artifacts for programming education. The system runs a complete Python runtime in the browser via Pyodide/WebAssembly, with no server-side infrastructure. The core contribution is a non-blocking execution model built on a dedicated Web Worker, which decouples computation from the UI thread and preserves interactivity during intensive tasks such as neural network training. This resolves the interfacefreezing limitation that affects all existing synchronous browser-based Python environments. CPIAE also integrates a context-aware Gemini 2.5 Flash AI assistance module that automatically builds large language model prompts from the student’s live code and runtime error output. A pedagogical 3D avatar with phoneme-synchronized speech synthesis narrates the AI responses. Three additional technical contributions round out the system: a decoupled module architecture with a shared EventTarget event bus; an import cache eliminating redundant library downloads; and a prompt engineering strategy grounding feedback in the live execution state. The system was deployed across a complete university neural computing course in Moodle. A pilot study with 15 undergraduate students showed that around 80% of runtime errors were resolved autonomously without instructor intervention. The single-artifact model was also verified on a smartphone, confirming viability on any standards-compliant browser. These results provide initial empirical evidence of the technical robustness and operational viability of edge-based execution combined with situated AI feedback.

title: CRIT AI 4.0: A Locally Deployable Artificial Intelligence System for Mortality Risk Stratification and Clinical Decision Support in Intensive Care Units
source: Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine
authors: Pratik kumar Mitra
keywords: mortality risk stratification; clinical decision support; intensive care unit; resource-limited settings; random forest; clinical scoring systems; nursing documentation; on-device large language models; cloud connectivity
topics: Machine Learning in Healthcare; Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education; Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
abstract: Background and aims: Intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in India remains high, with risk stratification inconsistently applied in resource-limited settings where AI-based decision support requires cloud connectivity unavailable to most Indian hospitals. We describe CRIT AI 4.0, a proof-of-concept, locally deployable, offline-capable AI-assisted decision support system for resource-constrained Indian ICUs. Patients and methods: A Python-based Windows application was developed, operating fully offline. A random forest (RF) classifier was trained on a synthetic dataset of 16,000 encounters across 17 disease categories with 37 input variables. Seven validated clinical scoring modules, six-shift fluid balance tracking, nursing documentation, and an on-device large language model (LLM) assistant were integrated, with no external data transmission. Results: = 3,200), the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.90 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.88-0.92), sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.77. All metrics reflect synthetic test-set performance only. Conclusion: CRIT AI 4.0 demonstrates the technical feasibility of offline artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented ICU decision support in resource-constrained settings. This is a proof-of-concept study; prospective validation is underway.

title: Design and Implementation of a MERN-Based AI Code Generation and Browser-Sandboxed Execution Platform Using Large Language Models
authors: Aryan Gawade; Tushar Chawre; Rushabh Gaur; Om Dhanke; Niranjan Kulkarni
keywords: AI-assisted code generation; large language models; Gemini; MERN stack
topics: Software Engineering Research; Mobile and Web Applications; Web Applications and Data Management
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into software development environments has significantly enhanced developer productivity through intelligent code generation. However, securely and efficiently executing AI-generated code remains a challenge due to potential security risks and infrastructure overhead. This paper presents the design and implementation of a MERN-based web application that integrates the Gemini LLM for multi-language code generation and utilizes browser-based Web Containers for secure sandboxed execution. The proposed system eliminates the need for local setup and server-side execution by leveraging client-side isolated runtime environments. Performance evaluation demonstrates reduced backend load and reliable multi-user execution.

title: Application and development of reinforcement learning in traffic signal control
source: Journal of Computer Science and Technology Studies
authors: Yuxiang Hong
keywords: reinforcement learning; traffic signal control; traffic congestion; multi-objective optimization; noise robustness; edge computing; interpretable reinforcement learning
topics: Traffic control and management; Traffic Prediction and Management Techniques; Reinforcement Learning in Robotics
abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, the traditional timing traffic signal control strategy is difficult to deal with the complex and variable nonlinear traffic flow. Reinforcement learning (RL) shows great potential in alleviating traffic congestion with its strong adaptive perception and optimization ability. However, reinforcement learning still faces many challenges in practical applications. This paper systematically reviews the latest research progress of reinforcement learning based traffic signal control (RL-TSC), focusing on control efficiency optimization, multi-objective constraints and overall architecture adjustment. Research shows that RL-TSC still has some problems, such as insufficient robustness to real-world noise, a lack of characterization of non-motor vehicle behavior, and a computing bottleneck of edge devices. The significance of this paper is to clearly point out the limitations and technical gaps of the current application in the rl-tsc field, and propose that the future research direction should be towards the interpretable RL, LLM hybrid architecture and global active scheduling, so as to provide theoretical guidance and forward-looking reference for the construction of a smart urban transportation system that takes into account safety, efficiency and sustainable development.

title: An LLM-empowered collaborative multi-agent framework for intermittent demand forecasting of large-scale spare parts in smart manufacturing
authors: Xiong Pan; Liping Zhang; Di Wu; Zikai Zhang; Minzhi Ruan; Yu Zhang
keywords: intermittent demand forecasting; spare parts demand; large language models; multi-agent systems; retrieval-augmented generation; anomaly detection; feature extraction; inventory optimization; smart manufacturing
topics: Forecasting Techniques and Applications; Time Series Analysis and Forecasting; Supply Chain and Inventory Management

title: A Privacy-Centric Framework for Autonomous Desktop Orchestration Using Local LLMs and Voice-Driven Workflows
source: Research Digest on Engineering Management and Social Innovations
authors: Y. Chiranjeevi Ashok Kumar; M. Hema Latha
keywords: local large language models; privacy-preserving AI; desktop automation; retrieval-augmented generation; wake word detection; speech-to-text; task automation; accessibility
topics: Speech and dialogue systems; Usability and User Interface Design; Speech Recognition and Synthesis
abstract: Today's desktop computer users often find their work interrupted by disjointed workflows and tedious, repetitive tasks—eating up nearly a third of their time. Although cloud-based voice assistants are available, they rarely integrate deeply with the operating system, tend to respond slowly, and can compromise user privacy. In this paper, we introduce "Your Own Jarvis": a privacy-first, always-on voice AI built to give users full control over their desktop and to automate everyday tasks. Unlike typical assistants, this system runs completely on your device. It uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) setup powered by fine-tuned Large Language Models like LLaMA or Mistral. For speech-to-text, it leverages OpenAI Whisper, and for wake-word detection, it uses Porcupine’s efficient technology. By connecting directly to your computer’s core features and using computer vision to understand what’s on your screen, the assistant can carry out complex tasks—whether that’s organising files, drafting emails, or running terminal commands for developers. Experimental results indicate a potential 60% reduction in routine task execution time and a 50% decrease in manual peripheral usage. The system achieves sub-500ms response latency without external data transmission, providing a secure, high-performance alternative for power users and individuals with accessibility needs. Our findings demonstrate that on-device AI can effectively bridge the gap between natural language intent and the complex execution of operating systems.

title: A Privacy-Preserving and Risk-Aware Data Exchange Model for Mobile Healthcare Applications Using SAP and AI-Based Threat Intelligence
source: Journal of Contemporary Science and Technology Management
authors: Akhilendra Gupta
keywords: mobile health apps; data exchange security; privacy-preserving data sharing; SAP integration; data minimization; pseudonymization; encryption; risk scoring; adaptive load balancing; prompt injection; electronic health records; wireless sensor networks; anomaly detection; credential theft; large language models
topics: Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Information and Cyber Security; Access Control and Trust
abstract: Mobile healthcare applications exchange sensitive data among patients, clinicians, connected devices, clinical systems, and enterprise platforms such as SAP, which manage procurement, inventory, billing, and claims. These exchanges face a fast-changing threat landscape that includes credential theft, malicious mobile applications, compromised devices, automated attacks on APIs, and manipulation of artificial intelligence (AI) features. Static security rules cannot keep pace. This article proposes a privacy-preserving and risk-aware data exchange model that combines data minimization, pseudonymization, consent enforcement, and encryption with AI-based threat intelligence. The model continuously gathers threat signals from internal telemetry and external intelligence sources, uses machine learning to correlate them, and translates the results into a real-time risk score for every exchange. That score drives graduated responses, from seamless access to step-up verification, restriction, and automated containment. SAP provides the governed integration backbone and the role-based user experience, while adaptive load balancing keeps controls effective under peak demand and attack. Building on research into secure mobile health data exchange, privacy-preserving access control for electronic health records, wireless sensor networks, adaptive load balancing, SAP Fiori and embedded analytics, large language model (LLM) integration with SAP, event-driven processing, anomaly detection, prompt-injection threats, and autonomous operations agents, the article describes the model’s architecture, threat intelligence pipeline, risk logic, use cases, evaluation metrics, and implementation roadmap.

title: A Privacy-Preserving Personal Knowledge Graph Using Local LLMs and Graph Databases
source: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
authors: SAKSHI VINOD CHOUDHARI SAKSHI VINOD CHOUDHARI
keywords: personal knowledge graphs; privacy preservation; on-device large language models; Neo4j; GraphRAG; Llama 2; Ollama; digital footprint; semantic reasoning; personal information management
topics: Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Privacy, Security, and Data Protection; Semantic Web and Ontologies
abstract: In the current era of digitization, people produce massive amounts of highly fragmented digital lifelogs, which are scattered over several isolated apps. Although the current solutions for cloudbased intelligent agents try to bring together all these data sets, they come at the cost of a significant breach of user privacy because these approaches necessitate sharing highly sensitive information with their cloud infrastructure. This paper introduces Eidomuse, an innovative, privacy-oriented personal knowledge database that integrates the benefits of a hybrid approach involving on-device Large Language Models (LLMs) and local graph databases to overcome this dilemma. Eidomuse automatically collects and semantically processes heterogeneous digital footprints, including Spotify playback logs, Google calendar events, Gmail correspondence, among others, into triples stored in a local Neo4j database. Leveraging Neo4j's index-free adjacency features allows mapping complex temporal dependencies between concepts from different domains. Additionally, Eidomuse uses a GraphRAG pipeline with quantized Llama-2 (7B parameters) deployed usingOllama that runs all natural language inferences and semantic reasoning offline, thus providing "zero-egress" privacy Conducted experimentally on the regular user model (16GB RAM), the robustness of the system can be confirmed through its ability to index more than 2,500 different elements using 21 distinct data sources.This was performed accurately within the local pipeline with inference latency averaging 4 to 6 seconds per complex question.Eventually, Eidomuse is presented as the paradigmatic solution for secure and context-specific personal data management and recall..

title: A process-centric review of large language models in graphical user interface testing: architectures, lifecycle impact, and challenges
authors: Phu Trong Mai; Ngo Tung Son; Vũ Trường Giang; Bui Hoang Viet; Le Ngoc Hai; Dinh Thanh Tung
keywords: large language models; GUI testing; LLM agents; test automation; semantic gap; Document Object Model; evaluation benchmark
topics: Software Testing and Debugging Techniques; Robotic Process Automation Applications; Software Engineering Research
abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) testing has historically struggled with the “semantic gap” between human understanding and machine execution. Large Language Models (LLMs) are now bridging this gap by enabling a transition from automating repetitive actions to automating cognitive processes. This article presents a process-centric review of 55 seminal studies published between January 2023 and July 2025 to systematize this rapid evolution. Unlike existing surveys that focus on isolated architectural elements, we analyze the integration of LLM agents across the entire testing lifecycle, from test design and scripting to execution, oracle verification, and maintenance. Our analysis reveals three key findings: (1) Architecture: Effective agents have converged on a “spatial-semantic” perception model, combining visual screenshots with Document Object Model (DOM) structures to ground high-level intent into precise actions. (2) Lifecycle Impact: The paradigm is shifting from rigid, specification-based script generation to autonomous, intent-driven exploration and self-healing maintenance via abstraction-concretization mechanisms. (3) Evaluation: While current benchmarks effectively measure task completion, a disconnect remains between academic prototypes and industrial requirements regarding reliability, cost, and latency. The article concludes by identifying critical gaps in business process testing and outlining a research roadmap to advance LLM-based testing from experimental prototypes to robust, enterprise-grade quality assurance solutions.

title: A Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications in the Internet of Things
authors: Vishwanath Kapoor; Mathew Wintters
keywords: Internet of Things; machine learning applications; predictive maintenance; failure prediction; Internet of Medical Things; smart cities; Industrial Internet of Things; Internet of Things security; intrusion detection; anomaly detection; federated learning; TinyML; large language models; agentic systems; data quality; privacy; resource-constrained devices
topics: Internet of Things and AI; IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Smart Agriculture and AI
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates vast amounts of data from billions of connected devices, and artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), has become the primary means of turning that data into useful action. This review surveys how AI and ML are applied across the IoT. The main families of learning techniques used in IoT settings are first outlined, including supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, deep learning, federated learning, and the on-device methods grouped under TinyML. The application of these techniques is then reviewed across several domains. Data analytics and predictive maintenance are considered first, where ML is used to forecast equipment failures and reduce downtime. Applications in healthcare, smart cities, and industry are then surveyed. The use of AI for IoT security, especially for intrusion and anomaly detection, is examined next, followed by the more recent use of AI, including large language model (LLM) based and agentic systems, for managing IoT networks. The main challenges are identified, including data quality, limited device resources, privacy, and the reliability of autonomous systems, and directions for future work are suggested. A broad and current map of where AI and ML are used in the IoT, and of the problems that remain, is intended to be provided for practitioners and researchers.

title: A Scalable and Low-Cost Mobile RAG Architecture for AI-Augmented Learning in Higher Education
authors: Rodolfo Bojorque; Andrea Plaza; Pilar Morquecho; Fernando Moscoso
keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; large language models; llamas; AI-augmented learning; higher education; low-income students; educational equity; academic performance; learner autonomy; low-resource computing
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Education; Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning; Online Learning and Analytics
abstract: This paper presents a scalable and low-cost Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture designed to enhance learning in university-level courses, with a particular focus on supporting students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable potential in educational contexts; however, their adoption is often limited by computational costs and the need for stable broadband access, issues that disproportionately affect low-income learners. To address this challenge, we propose a lightweight, mobile, and friendly RAG system that integrates the LLaMA language model with the Milvus vector database, enabling efficient on device retrieval and context-grounded generation using only modest hardware resources. The system was implemented in a university-level Data Mining course and evaluated over four semesters using a quasi-experimental design with randomized assignment to experimental and control groups. Students in the experimental group had voluntary access to the RAG assistant, while the control group followed the same instructional schedule without exposure to the tool. Results show statistically significant improvements in academic performance for the experimental group, with p < 0.01 in the first semester and p < 0.001 in the subsequent three semesters. Effect sizes, measured using Hedges g to account for small cohort sizes, increased from 0.56 (moderate) to 1.52 (extremely large), demonstrating a clear and growing pedagogical impact over time. Qualitative feedback further indicates increased learner autonomy, confidence, and engagement. These findings highlight the potential of mobile RAG architectures to deliver equitable, high-quality AI support to students regardless of socioeconomic status. The proposed solution offers a practical engineering pathway for institutions seeking inclusive, scalable, and resource-efficient approaches to AI-enhanced education.

title: A study of agentic AI in Business Automation
source: International Journal of Versatile Research and Analysis
authors: Ayush Singh; Mr. Sarvesh Kumar Srivastava; Ashwani Kumar
keywords: agentic AI; business process automation; robotic process automation; large language models; tool use; agent orchestration; query resolution; tool registry; cost modeling
topics: Robotic Process Automation Applications; Artificial Intelligence Applications; Business Process Modeling and Analysis
abstract: —For years, business process automation has depended on Robotic Process Automation (RPA), which performs scripted steps dependably but loses accuracy when documents, layouts or rules shift. Agentic AI replaces the fixed script with a goal-oriented cycle in which a large language model (LLM) plans, invokes tools, inspects what comes back and adjusts. This paper examines that change through a representative back-office task: vendor invoice processing together with query resolution. We (i) survey the literature on agents, tool use, orchestration and benchmarks, (ii) put forward a layered, governance-first architecture built from an orchestrator, narrowly scoped worker agents, a schema-validated tool registry, memory and human-approval gates, (iii) set it against RPA in terms of architecture, performance and cost, and (iv) specify an 80-case evaluation protocol. Figures reported in earlier work show that RPA stays faster, and at least as dependable, on stable tasks, whereas an LLM agent reduced build effort by roughly 4–16× and coped with layout variation. A parametric model calibrated on those figures projects that agents become cheaper than RPA once about 20–30% of volume is non-standard, that token spend accounts for less than 16% of effective cost, and that a hybrid of RPA and an agent is the least expensive option. These projections come from a model rather than from measurement; evaluating the prototype is planned future work.

title: A Study on Locally Runnable Large Language Models for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
authors: Mehadi Hasan Shawon; Prashant Kumar
keywords: bearing fault diagnosis; large language models; Ollama; small language models; vibration characteristics; prognostics and health management; few-shot prompting; model benchmarking; rotating machinery; Paderborn bearing dataset; CWRU bearing dataset
topics: Machine Fault Diagnosis Techniques; Fault Detection and Control Systems; Topic Modeling
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can perform prognostics and health management (PHM) tasks such as bearing fault diagnosis, but most published systems rely on large, paid, cloud-hosted models that a small or medium enterprise (SME) cannot self-host. The diagnostic accuracy that can be achieved on free, offline, commodity hardware is a practical question. Using an execution-based evaluation (Pass@1, Pass all 3, macro F1), this paper benchmarks eight small, publicly accessible, locally runnable LLMs (1B–9B parameters, via Ollama) on vibration-derived features for three-class bearing fault diagnosis (Healthy, Outer race, and Inner race). The proposed work is evaluated on three independent datasets, Paderborn, CWRU, and HUST, across a 0–5-shot ablation and at two decoding temperatures to separate accuracy from reliability. The findings replicate across all three datasets, namely, a model-capability gate that only models near 7B parameters and above clears the majority-class floor; few-shot prompting is non-monotonic; accuracy and reliability are distinct axes; and a single free model, gemma2:9b (5.4 GB), is the most accurate and among the most reliable, with no task-specific training. We further propose ensemble agreement gating, a training-free reliability rule that withholds predictions when several free local models disagree, raising accuracy on the answered subset (e.g., 0.77 → 0.87 on Paderborn). In a head-to-head on identical prompts and data, the free local models match a current frontier model in the settings tested at zero cost and fully offline, and we characterize where such a training-free local approach is and is not appropriate for resource-constrained operators of rotating machinery. On the same features, however, a simple supervised baseline such as logistic regression, and even an untrained physics rule, outperform all eight LLMs, so we present this as a cautionary benchmark: the contribution of the free local approach is training-free deployment and a reliability gating rule, not classification accuracy.

title: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF ENERGY EFFICIENT DEPLOYMENT STRATEGIES FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN REAL WORLD APPLICATIONS
source: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)
authors: Sweta Kumari; Shashank Swami
keywords: large language models; energy-efficient deployment; inference optimization; green AI; edge-cloud computing; model compression; parameter-efficient fine-tuning; conditional computation; energy consumption; on-device inference
topics: Green IT and Sustainability; Energy Efficiency in Computing; Advanced Neural Network Applications
abstract: The widespread use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in practice has become an issue of mounting concern regarding energy usage and sustainability, as inference loads rapidly begin to comprise a larger portion of the total cost of the AI systems. It is a review of the literature published on energy-efficient deployment strategies of LLMs addressing the energy challenges at the deployment stage, methods of optimizing models at the deployment stage, and system-level and hardware-aware serving strategies. The inference-focused workloads, heterogeneity in the infrastructure between the cloud, edge, and on-device, and overheads at the system level are discussed as the main contributors to deployment-time energy wastefulness. The review also evaluates the use of model compression, parameter-efficient adaptation, conditional computation, adaptive serving models, and accelerator-aware execution to reduce energy expenditure within real-world restrictions. In general, the article points to the necessity of more coherent and comprehensive deployment models and universalized energy assessment procedures as the only way to make LLMs usable in large-scale production settings in a scalable and sustainable manner. Keywords: Large Language Models; Energy-Efficient Deployment; Inference Optimization; Green AI; Edge–Cloud Computing

title: A Systematic Taxonomy of Large Language Model Inference Optimization: Bridging Model-Level and API-Layer Latency Reduction Strategies
authors: Yao-Liang Chung
keywords: latency reduction; post-training quantization; AWQ; GPTQ; GGUF; model compression; model routing; prompt caching; edge deployment; autonomous agents; 6G; memory efficiency; inference throughput
topics: Advanced Neural Network Applications; Topic Modeling; Natural Language Processing Techniques
abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) as autonomous agents in next generation infrastructures, such as Agentic AI-Native 6G networks, introduces severe latency, memory, and operational cost bottlenecks.Existing optimization approaches frequently treat model compression and system orchestration in isolation, failing to adequately address the multidimensional constraints of modern production environments.This paper presents a systematic, multi criteria taxonomy of LLM inference optimization, bridging granular model level compression techniques with macro level API-layer orchestration strategies.We conduct a rigorous comparative analysis of post training quantization algorithms specifically highlighting activationaware methods like AWQ alongside GPTQ and GGUF evaluating their trade offs across memory efficiency, inference throughput, and predictive quality.Our findings reveal that deployment efficiency is not solely dictated by numerical precision but is fundamentally a co-design problem requiring optimized hardware kernels and adaptive, importance aware parameter protection.Furthermore, we demonstrate that systemlevel interventions, such as intelligent model routing, prompt caching, and deterministic decoupling, yield immediate latency reductions without altering underlying model weights.Ultimately, this study provides a comprehensive, scenario based decision framework for matching specific quantization algorithms and APIlayer strategies to distinct deployment environments, ranging from high throughput GPU serving to resourceconstrained edge devices and safety critical autonomous systems.By unifying these perspectives, we establish a foundational guide for practitioners aiming to build reliable, high performance inference pipelines that ensure scalable and economically sustainable AI integration across diverse industrial domains.

title: A Unified Privacy-Preserving AI Assistant Integrating Conversational AI, Legal Advisory, and Document Intelligence
source: International Journal of Technology & Emerging Research
authors: Bhagyashree Sanjay Deshmukhe; Manasi Mahavir Kurade; Arpita Dhanpal Devmore; Prasanna Sanjay Adake; Girish Rahul Bhosale; Shrenik R. Patil
